family.description: This domain is found linked to a wide range of non-homologous domains in a variety of bacteria. It has been shown to be homologous to the adenylyl cyclase catalytic domain [[cite:PUB00007061]] and has diguanylate cyclase activity [[cite:PUB00016966]]. This observation correlates with the functional information available on two GGDEF-containing proteins, namely diguanylate cyclase and phosphodiesterase A of Acetobacter xylinum, both of which regulate the turnover of cyclic diguanosine monophosphate. In the WspR protein of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, the GGDEF domain acts as a diguanylate cyclase, PDB:3bre, when the whole molecule appears to form a tetramer consisting of two symmetrically-related dimers representing a biological unit. The active site is the GGD/EF motif, buried in the structure, and the cyclic dimeric guanosine monophosphate (c-di-GMP) bind to the inhibitory-motif RxxD on the surface. The enzyme thus catalyses the cyclisation of two guanosine triphosphate (GTP) molecules to one c-di-GMP molecule [[cite:PUB00016971],[cite:PUB00109145],[cite:PUB00050740]].
family.name: Diguanylate cyclase, GGDEF domain

causal_graphs.context: The 2004 Genes & Development TLC assays use 50 uL, 75 mM Tris pH 7.8, 250 mM NaCl, 25 mM KCl, 10 mM MgCl2 and 100 uM GTP. Figure 5B uses 50 ug PleD; Figures 6A and 7A use 25 ug. The TLC assay temperature is not specified in the inspected methods; the separate HPLC protocol is 90 min at 25 C. GTP and magnesium are joint reaction inputs.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure 5B-C includes the no-protein control and product spectrum; the purified-protein result is distinct from Figure 5A cell extracts. Table 2 identifies pCC2.
evidence.snippet: Cyclic-di-GMP is produced by purified PleD protein.

evidence.explanation: Exact reference-sequence comparison supports the family mapping; source-strain ambiguity is retained rather than counted as two experiments.
evidence.snippet: Q9A5I5 Pfam interval: PF00990 at 289-447, inclusive.

edges.mechanism: Purified PleD converts GTP into a product identified as c-di-GMP by TLC, HPLC and the product mass spectrum. The graph records net catalysis, not an atomistic condensation trajectory.
edges.subject: pled-dgc-activity

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure 6A compares added c-di-GMP with the no-added-nucleotide condition. Unlabeled GTP bars also involve tracer dilution and are not used to infer this edge. The later allosteric interpretation is retained separately.

edges.mechanism: Adding chemically synthesized c-di-GMP at 10 or 100 uM reduces the initial labeled-product formation rate with 100 uM GTP. This establishes product inhibition without assigning a competitive active-site mechanism.
edges.subject: cyclic-digmp

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure 7A and its caption support the combined-treatment effect and D53N control. This is the measured activity response, not direct visualization of the proposed domain rearrangement or a cellular phosphorelay.

edges.mechanism: Joint addition of 12.5 ug soluble DivJ and 200 uM ATP increases the WT PleD initial rate. Single-addition controls and D53N PleD do not show this stimulation; the inputs are not represented as independently sufficient causes.
edges.subject: divj-atp-addition

causal_graphs.family_mapping: PleD references Q9A5I5 (CB15, CC_2462) and B8GZM2 (NA1000/CB15N, CCNA_02546) have identical 454-aa sequences, both version 1. Q9A5I5 maps to PF00990 at 289-447. Deposited 1W25 matches native residues 2-454 plus His6, with CB15 source taxonomy but a SIFTS B8GZM2 mapping. The exact pCC2 cloning template remains unverified; species-level taxonomy avoids conflating the two reference strains.
causal_graphs.feedback_explanation: PleD makes c-di-GMP, and added c-di-GMP decreases PleD's initial product-formation rate in a separate assay. These experimentally supported directions define negative product feedback under the stated in-vitro conditions; they do not establish a cellular steady state or measured oscillation.
causal_graphs.limitations: Separate compatible biochemical assays support the graph, not a single measured feedback trajectory. Product inhibition is qualitative here; the later PNAS noncompetitive interpretation supersedes the earlier competitive-binding suggestion, but its supplementary fit was not inspected. DivJ-plus-ATP stimulation does not itself resolve phosphorylation, dimerization and domain-motion microsteps. The exact DivJ fragment boundaries and pCC2 template sequence remain unverified. No family-wide catalytic competence or cell-cycle phenotype is inferred.
